properties.statement: A function table loads iff axis names and outputs are unique, interpolation matches the axis count, every axis is NaN-free, strictly increasing with ≥ 2 values, data has the implied nesting and no NaN leaf (Q-9), and any shape assertion equals the implied shape.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (T : Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable), Esm.Closed.Tables.validateTable T = Except.ok () ↔ Esm.Closed.Tables.TableValid T
properties.note: Retired by ruling Q-109 (2026-10-27): its statement is about a table already holding Num values, where only NaN can be non-finite; the ruled spec names NaN, +Inf and -Inf. Still proven of FTable. Superseded by P-tables-raw-valid-iff.

properties.statement: Every rejection of a table names a violated condition with its §9.5.5 code.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (T : Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable) (c : Esm.Closed.Code), Esm.Closed.Tables.validateTable T = Except.error c → c = "table_axis_duplicate_name" ∧ ¬(List.map (fun (x : Esm.Closed.Tables.Axis) => x.name) T.axes).Nodup ∨ (c = "table_outputs_duplicate_name" ∧ ∃ (os : List String), T.outputs = Option.some os ∧ ¬os.Nodup) ∨ c = "table_interpolation_axes_mismatch" ∧ Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable.arityOk T.interpolation T.axes.length = Bool.false ∨ (c = "table_axis_nan" ∧ ∃ a ∈ T.axes, ∃ x ∈ a.values, x.isNaN = Bool.true) ∨ (c = "table_axis_non_monotonic" ∧ ∃ a ∈ T.axes, ∃ (r : List ℝ), a.values = List.map Esm.Closed.Num.fin r ∧ ¬List.Pairwise (fun (x1 x2 : ℝ) => x1 < x2) r) ∨ (c = "table_axis_too_short" ∧ ∃ a ∈ T.axes, a.values.length < (2 : ℕ)) ∨ (c = "table_outputs_length_mismatch" ∧ ∃ (os : List String) (xs : List Esm.Closed.Tables.Nested), T.outputs = Option.some os ∧ T.data = Esm.Closed.Tables.Nested.node xs ∧ xs.length ≠ os.length) ∨ c = "table_data_shape_mismatch" ∧ (T.data.hasShape T.expectedShape = Bool.false ∨ ∃ (sh : List ℕ), T.shape = Option.some sh ∧ sh ≠ T.expectedShape) ∨ c = "table_data_nan" ∧ T.data.anyNaN = Bool.true
properties.supersedes: P-tables-code-sound, whose statement named the non-spec marker unspecified:table_axis_too_short; Q-105 named the code table_axis_too_short.
properties.note: Retired by ruling Q-109 (2026-10-27): its table_axis_nan / table_data_nan disjuncts name NaN only. Still proven of FTable. Superseded by P-tables-raw-ladder.

properties.statement: Q-4: once the name and arity checks pass, a NaN in any axis is table_axis_nan (before table_axis_non_monotonic).
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (T : Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable), (List.map (fun (x : Esm.Closed.Tables.Axis) => x.name) T.axes).Nodup → (∀ (os : List String), T.outputs = Option.some os → os.Nodup) → Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable.arityOk T.interpolation T.axes.length = Bool.true → (∃ a ∈ T.axes, ∃ x ∈ a.values, x.isNaN = Bool.true) → Esm.Closed.Tables.validateTable T = Except.error "table_axis_nan"
properties.note: Retired by ruling Q-109 (2026-10-27): the precedence now covers every non-finite axis value, not only NaN. Still proven of FTable. Superseded by P-tables-axis-nonfinite-precedence.

properties.statement: Step 1: table_axis_duplicate_name exactly when two axes share a name.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (T : Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable), Esm.Closed.Tables.validateTable T = Except.error "table_axis_duplicate_name" ↔ Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.axisDupName T

properties.statement: Step 2: table_outputs_duplicate_name exactly when two outputs share a name and step 1 passes.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (T : Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable), Esm.Closed.Tables.validateTable T = Except.error "table_outputs_duplicate_name" ↔ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.axisDupName T ∧ Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.outputsDupName T

properties.statement: Step 3: table_interpolation_axes_mismatch exactly when interpolation and axis count disagree and steps 1-2 pass.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (T : Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable), Esm.Closed.Tables.validateTable T = Except.error "table_interpolation_axes_mismatch" ↔ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.axisDupName T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.outputsDupName T ∧ Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.arity T

properties.statement: Step 4: table_axis_nan exactly when some axis holds a NaN and steps 1-3 pass.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (T : Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable), Esm.Closed.Tables.validateTable T = Except.error "table_axis_nan" ↔ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.axisDupName T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.outputsDupName T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.arity T ∧ Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.axisNaN T
properties.note: Retired by ruling Q-109 (2026-10-27): step 4 is a non-finite axis value (NaN or ±Inf). Still proven of FTable. Superseded by P-tables-order-axis-nonfinite.

properties.statement: Step 5: table_axis_non_monotonic exactly when some (NaN-free) axis is not strictly increasing and steps 1-4 pass.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (T : Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable), Esm.Closed.Tables.validateTable T = Except.error "table_axis_non_monotonic" ↔ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.axisDupName T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.outputsDupName T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.arity T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.axisNaN T ∧ Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.axisNonMonotonic T

properties.statement: Step 7: table_outputs_length_mismatch exactly when outputs is declared, data is an array of another length, and steps 1-6 pass.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (T : Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable), Esm.Closed.Tables.validateTable T = Except.error "table_outputs_length_mismatch" ↔ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.axisDupName T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.outputsDupName T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.arity T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.axisNaN T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.axisNonMonotonic T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.axisTooShort T ∧ Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.outputsLength T

properties.statement: Steps 8 and 10: table_data_shape_mismatch exactly when the nesting of data is wrong and steps 1-7 pass, or the shape assertion is wrong and steps 1-9 pass.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (T : Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable), Esm.Closed.Tables.validateTable T = Except.error "table_data_shape_mismatch" ↔ (¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.axisDupName T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.outputsDupName T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.arity T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.axisNaN T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.axisNonMonotonic T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.axisTooShort T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.outputsLength T ∧ Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.nesting T) ∨ (¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.axisDupName T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.outputsDupName T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.arity T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.axisNaN T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.axisNonMonotonic T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.axisTooShort T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.outputsLength T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.nesting T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.dataNaN T ∧ Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.shapeAssertion T)

properties.statement: Step 9: table_data_nan exactly when a data leaf is NaN and steps 1-8 pass.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (T : Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable), Esm.Closed.Tables.validateTable T = Except.error "table_data_nan" ↔ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.axisDupName T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.outputsDupName T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.arity T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.axisNaN T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.axisNonMonotonic T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.axisTooShort T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.outputsLength T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.nesting T ∧ Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.dataNaN T
properties.note: Retired by ruling Q-109 (2026-10-27): step 9 is a non-finite leaf (NaN or ±Inf). Still proven of FTable. Superseded by P-tables-order-data-nonfinite.

properties.statement: Q-11: a table_lookup with non-empty args is table_lookup_args_nonempty.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (tables : List (String × Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable)) (env : String → Esm.Closed.Num) (tid : String) (axes : List (String × Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr)) (out : Option Esm.Closed.Tables.OutSel) (args : List Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr), args ≠ [] → Esm.Closed.Tables.eval tables env (Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr.lookup tid axes out args) = Except.error "table_lookup_args_nonempty"
properties.note: Retired by ruling Q-107 (2026-10-27): a table_lookup is checked unknown table, then the ten checks of its table, then args. Refuted at a lookup with non-empty args naming an undeclared table (table_lookup_unknown_table). Superseded by P-tables-lookup-check-order.

properties.statement: A reference to an undeclared table is table_lookup_unknown_table.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (tables : List (String × Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable)) (env : String → Esm.Closed.Num) (tid : String) (axes : List (String × Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr)) (out : Option Esm.Closed.Tables.OutSel), List.lookup tid tables = Option.none → Esm.Closed.Tables.eval tables env (Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr.lookup tid axes out []) = Except.error "table_lookup_unknown_table"

properties.statement: On a valid table, axis keys that are not exactly its axis names are table_lookup_axis_name_mismatch.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (tables : List (String × Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable)) (env : String → Esm.Closed.Num) (tid : String) (axes : List (String × Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr)) (out : Option Esm.Closed.Tables.OutSel) (T : Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable), List.lookup tid tables = Option.some T → Esm.Closed.Tables.validateTable T = Except.ok () → (¬∀ (k : String), k ∈ List.map Prod.fst axes ↔ k ∈ List.map (fun (x : Esm.Closed.Tables.Axis) => x.name) T.axes) → Esm.Closed.Tables.eval tables env (Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr.lookup tid axes out []) = Except.error "table_lookup_axis_name_mismatch"

properties.statement: Q-12: an omitted output is output 0, with or without outputs.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (T : Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable), Esm.Closed.Tables.resolveOutput T Option.none = Esm.Closed.Tables.resolveOutput T (Option.some (Esm.Closed.Tables.OutSel.idx (0 : ℕ)))

properties.statement: Q-10: without outputs, the only valid output is 0; a string output is out of range.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (T : Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable), T.outputs = Option.none → ∀ (n : ℕ) (s : String), (Esm.Closed.Tables.resolveOutput T (Option.some (Esm.Closed.Tables.OutSel.idx n)) = if n = (0 : ℕ) then Except.ok (0 : ℕ) else Except.error "table_lookup_output_out_of_range") ∧ Esm.Closed.Tables.resolveOutput T (Option.some (Esm.Closed.Tables.OutSel.name s)) = Except.error "table_lookup_output_out_of_range"

properties.statement: With outputs, an integer must be < len(outputs) and a string must be one of them (its first position); otherwise table_lookup_output_out_of_range.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (T : Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable) (os : List String), T.outputs = Option.some os → ∀ (n : ℕ) (s : String), (Esm.Closed.Tables.resolveOutput T (Option.some (Esm.Closed.Tables.OutSel.idx n)) = if n < os.length then Except.ok n else Except.error "table_lookup_output_out_of_range") ∧ (s ∉ os → Esm.Closed.Tables.resolveOutput T (Option.some (Esm.Closed.Tables.OutSel.name s)) = Except.error "table_lookup_output_out_of_range") ∧ ∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i < os.length), os[i] = s → (∀ (j : ℕ) (hj : j < i), os[j] ≠ s) → Esm.Closed.Tables.resolveOutput T (Option.some (Esm.Closed.Tables.OutSel.name s)) = Except.ok i

properties.statement: For out_of_bounds clamp, evaluating the §9.5.3 lowered tree equals evaluating the table_lookup, for linear, bilinear and nearest (Q-10 slice, Q-13 nearest), whenever the lookup lowers and its inputs are scalars.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (tables : List (String × Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable)) (env : String → Esm.Closed.Num) (tid : String) (axes : List (String × Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr)) (out : Option Esm.Closed.Tables.OutSel) (args : List Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr) (e : Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr), Esm.Closed.Tables.lower tables tid axes out args = Except.ok e → (∀ p ∈ axes, ∃ (v : Esm.Closed.Num), Esm.Closed.Tables.eval tables env p.2 = Except.ok (Esm.Closed.Tables.Val.num v)) → (∀ (T : Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable), List.lookup tid tables = Option.some T → T.outOfBounds = Esm.Closed.Tables.OOB.clamp) → Esm.Closed.Tables.eval tables env e = Esm.Closed.Tables.eval tables env (Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr.lookup tid axes out args)

properties.statement: out_of_bounds error: the lookup raises table_lookup_out_of_bounds exactly when an input is strictly outside its axis, otherwise equals the lowered tree.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (tables : List (String × Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable)) (env : String → Esm.Closed.Num) (tid : String) (axes : List (String × Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr)) (out : Option Esm.Closed.Tables.OutSel) (args : List Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr) (e : Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr), Esm.Closed.Tables.lower tables tid axes out args = Except.ok e → (∀ p ∈ axes, ∃ (v : Esm.Closed.Num), Esm.Closed.Tables.eval tables env p.2 = Except.ok (Esm.Closed.Tables.Val.num v)) → ∃ (T : Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable) (xs : List Esm.Closed.Num), List.lookup tid tables = Option.some T ∧ List.mapM (fun (a : Esm.Closed.Tables.Axis) => (Esm.Closed.Tables.eval tables env ((List.lookup a.name axes).getD (Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr.lit Esm.Closed.Num.nan))).bind Esm.Closed.Tables.Val.asNum) T.axes = Except.ok xs ∧ Esm.Closed.Tables.eval tables env (Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr.lookup tid axes out args) = if (Decidable.decide (T.outOfBounds = Esm.Closed.Tables.OOB.error) && Esm.Closed.Tables.anyOutside T xs) = Bool.true then Except.error Esm.Closed.Tables.Codes.lookupOutOfBounds else Esm.Closed.Tables.eval tables env e

properties.statement: 'Outside' is strictly below the first knot or strictly above the last (end knots are in range).
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (r : List ℝ), (1 : ℕ) ≤ r.length → ∀ (x : ℝ), Esm.Closed.Tables.outside (List.map Esm.Closed.Num.fin r) (Esm.Closed.Num.fin x) = Bool.true ↔ x < r.getD (0 : ℕ) (0 : ℝ) ∨ r.getD (r.length - (1 : ℕ)) (0 : ℝ) < x

properties.statement: A NaN query is not out of bounds.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (ax : List Esm.Closed.Num), Esm.Closed.Tables.outside ax Esm.Closed.Num.nan = Bool.false

properties.statement: The §9.5.3 nearest tree ifelse(x==x, index(D, ifelse(A[hi]−x < x−A[lo], hi, lo)), x), j = searchsorted(x, A), lo = max(j−1, 1), hi = min(j, N), evaluated with EXACT arithmetic, is the value at the nearest knot (ties low, clamped), and NaN for a NaN query.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (tables : List (String × Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable)) (env : String → Esm.Closed.Num) (v : List Esm.Closed.Num) (r0 : List ℝ), List.Pairwise (fun (x1 x2 : ℝ) => x1 < x2) r0 → (2 : ℕ) ≤ r0.length → v.length = r0.length → ∀ (xe : Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr) (x0 : Esm.Closed.Num), Esm.Closed.Tables.eval tables env xe = Except.ok (Esm.Closed.Tables.Val.num x0) → Esm.Closed.Tables.eval tables env (Esm.Closed.Tables.nearestTree (Esm.Closed.Tables.ofVec v) (List.map Esm.Closed.Num.fin r0) xe) = Except.ok (Esm.Closed.Tables.Val.num (Esm.Closed.Tables.nearest v (List.map Esm.Closed.Num.fin r0) x0))

properties.statement: With exact distances, the nearest knot (least argmin, ties low) is hi when A[hi] − x < x − A[lo] and lo otherwise, lo/hi the bracketing knots of searchsorted.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (a : List ℝ), List.Pairwise (fun (x1 x2 : ℝ) => x1 < x2) a → (2 : ℕ) ≤ a.length → ∀ (x : ℝ), Esm.Closed.Tables.nearestIdx a x = if a.getD (Min.min (List.findIdx (fun (b : ℝ) => Decidable.decide (x ≤ b)) a) (a.length - (1 : ℕ))) (0 : ℝ) - x < x - a.getD (List.findIdx (fun (b : ℝ) => Decidable.decide (x ≤ b)) a - (1 : ℕ)) (0 : ℝ) then Min.min (List.findIdx (fun (b : ℝ) => Decidable.decide (x ≤ b)) a) (a.length - (1 : ℕ)) else List.findIdx (fun (b : ℝ) => Decidable.decide (x ≤ b)) a - (1 : ℕ)

properties.statement: Q-13 for the §9.5.3 tree with its two subtractions in binary64: for every strictly increasing axis of doubles and double query it selects the true nearest knot. REFUTED: axis [−1, 1], x = 2^−60; knot 1 is nearer but 1 ⊖ x = x ⊖ (−1) = 1, so the tree returns knot −1.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (a : List ℝ) (x : ℝ), List.Pairwise (fun (p q : ℝ) => p < q) a → 2 ≤ a.length → (∀ b ∈ a, Esm.F64.Repr b) → Esm.F64.Repr x → Esm.Closed.Tables.nearest64 a x = Esm.Closed.Tables.nearestIdx a x

properties.statement: What holds in binary64: the tree selects the true nearest knot, except that when the upper bracketing knot is strictly nearer it may select the lower one, and only when the two exact distances differ by at most ulp(x − A[lo]); it never errs toward the upper knot.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (a : List ℝ), List.Pairwise (fun (x1 x2 : ℝ) => x1 < x2) a → (2 : ℕ) ≤ a.length → ∀ (x : ℝ), Esm.Closed.Tables.nearest64 a x = Esm.Closed.Tables.nearestIdx a x ∨ Esm.Closed.Tables.nearest64 a x = Esm.Closed.Tables.nlo a x ∧ Esm.Closed.Tables.nearestIdx a x = Esm.Closed.Tables.nhi a x ∧ (0 : ℝ) < x - a.getD (Esm.Closed.Tables.nlo a x) (0 : ℝ) - (a.getD (Esm.Closed.Tables.nhi a x) (0 : ℝ) - x) ∧ x - a.getD (Esm.Closed.Tables.nlo a x) (0 : ℝ) - (a.getD (Esm.Closed.Tables.nhi a x) (0 : ℝ) - x) ≤ Esm.F64.ulp (x - a.getD (Esm.Closed.Tables.nlo a x) (0 : ℝ))

properties.statement: Q-13: the nearest index is a knot (clamping), minimizes |x − knot|, and is strictly closer than every lower knot (ties go to the lower knot).
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (r : List ℝ), List.Pairwise (fun (x1 x2 : ℝ) => x1 < x2) r → (1 : ℕ) ≤ r.length → ∀ (x : ℝ), Esm.Closed.Tables.nearestIdx r x < r.length ∧ (∀ j < r.length, |x - r.getD (Esm.Closed.Tables.nearestIdx r x) (0 : ℝ)| ≤ |x - r.getD j (0 : ℝ)|) ∧ ∀ j < Esm.Closed.Tables.nearestIdx r x, |x - r.getD (Esm.Closed.Tables.nearestIdx r x) (0 : ℝ)| < |x - r.getD j (0 : ℝ)|

properties.statement: Q-13: the first midpoint ≥ x locates the nearest knot, ties low.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (r : List ℝ), List.Pairwise (fun (x1 x2 : ℝ) => x1 < x2) r → (1 : ℕ) ≤ r.length → ∀ (x : ℝ), List.findIdx (fun (m : ℝ) => Decidable.decide (x ≤ m)) (Esm.Closed.Tables.midsR r) = Esm.Closed.Tables.nearestIdx r x

properties.statement: §9.5.3's current nearest lowering index(data, searchsorted(x, axis)) returns the value at the nearest knot. REFUTED: axis [0, 10], data [1, 2], x = 1 gives 2, not 1.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (v : List Esm.Closed.Num) (r : List ℝ) (x : ℝ), List.Pairwise (fun (a b : ℝ) => a < b) r → 2 ≤ r.length → v.length = r.length → Esm.Closed.Tables.eval [] (fun _ => Esm.Closed.Num.nan) (Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr.index [Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr.const (Esm.Closed.Tables.ofVec v), Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr.fn "interp.searchsorted" [Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr.lit (Esm.Closed.Num.fin x), Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr.const (Esm.Closed.Tables.ofVec (r.map Esm.Closed.Num.fin))]]) = Except.ok (Esm.Closed.Tables.Val.num (Esm.Closed.Tables.nearest v (r.map Esm.Closed.Num.fin) (Esm.Closed.Num.fin x)))

properties.statement: Step 6 (Q-105): table_axis_too_short exactly when some axis has fewer than 2 values and steps 1-5 pass.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (T : Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable), Esm.Closed.Tables.validateTable T = Except.error "table_axis_too_short" ↔ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.axisDupName T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.outputsDupName T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.arity T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.axisNaN T ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.axisNonMonotonic T ∧ Esm.Closed.Tables.Rule.axisTooShort T

properties.statement: Q-105 + Q-109: the checks on a table as read (values finite, NaN, +Inf or -Inf) are the ten §9.5.5 rules read in order, the first broken rule naming the code; a non-finite axis value is table_axis_nan (step 4), a non-finite data leaf table_data_nan (step 9).
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (R : Esm.Closed.Tables.RTable Esm.Closed.Tables.Lit), open Classical in (Esm.Closed.Tables.validateRaw R = if Esm.Closed.Tables.RRule.axisDupName R then Except.error "table_axis_duplicate_name" else if Esm.Closed.Tables.RRule.outputsDupName R then Except.error "table_outputs_duplicate_name" else if Esm.Closed.Tables.RRule.arity R then Except.error "table_interpolation_axes_mismatch" else if Esm.Closed.Tables.RRule.axisNonFinite R then Except.error "table_axis_nan" else if Esm.Closed.Tables.RRule.axisNonMonotonic R then Except.error "table_axis_non_monotonic" else if Esm.Closed.Tables.RRule.axisTooShort R then Except.error "table_axis_too_short" else if Esm.Closed.Tables.RRule.outputsLength R then Except.error "table_outputs_length_mismatch" else if Esm.Closed.Tables.RRule.nesting R then Except.error "table_data_shape_mismatch" else if Esm.Closed.Tables.RRule.dataNonFinite R then Except.error "table_data_nan" else if Esm.Closed.Tables.RRule.shapeAssertion R then Except.error "table_data_shape_mismatch" else Except.ok ())
properties.supersedes: P-tables-code-sound-q105, whose table_axis_nan / table_data_nan disjuncts named NaN only (Q-109).

properties.statement: Step 4 (Q-109): table_axis_nan exactly when some axis holds a non-finite value (NaN, +Inf or -Inf) and steps 1-3 pass.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (R : Esm.Closed.Tables.RTable Esm.Closed.Tables.Lit), Esm.Closed.Tables.validateRaw R = Except.error "table_axis_nan" ↔ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.RRule.axisDupName R ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.RRule.outputsDupName R ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.RRule.arity R ∧ Esm.Closed.Tables.RRule.axisNonFinite R

properties.statement: Step 9 (Q-109): table_data_nan exactly when a data leaf is not finite (NaN, +Inf or -Inf) and steps 1-8 pass.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (R : Esm.Closed.Tables.RTable Esm.Closed.Tables.Lit), Esm.Closed.Tables.validateRaw R = Except.error "table_data_nan" ↔ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.RRule.axisDupName R ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.RRule.outputsDupName R ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.RRule.arity R ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.RRule.axisNonFinite R ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.RRule.axisNonMonotonic R ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.RRule.axisTooShort R ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.RRule.outputsLength R ∧ ¬Esm.Closed.Tables.RRule.nesting R ∧ Esm.Closed.Tables.RRule.dataNonFinite R

properties.statement: Q-4 + Q-109: once the name and arity checks pass, an axis holding a non-finite value (NaN, +Inf or -Inf) is table_axis_nan, whatever its other entries.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (R : Esm.Closed.Tables.RTable Esm.Closed.Tables.Lit), (List.map (fun (x : Esm.Closed.Tables.RAxis Esm.Closed.Tables.Lit) => x.name) R.axes).Nodup → (∀ (os : List String), R.outputs = Option.some os → os.Nodup) → Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable.arityOk R.interpolation R.axes.length = Bool.true → (∃ a ∈ R.axes, ∃ x ∈ a.values, x.isFinite = Bool.false) → Esm.Closed.Tables.validateRaw R = Except.error "table_axis_nan"

properties.statement: Q-109: a table as read passes the checks iff axis names and outputs are unique, interpolation matches the axis count, every axis is finite and strictly increasing with ≥ 2 values, data has the implied nesting and every leaf finite, and any shape assertion equals the implied shape.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (R : Esm.Closed.Tables.RTable Esm.Closed.Tables.Lit), Esm.Closed.Tables.validateRaw R = Except.ok () ↔ Esm.Closed.Tables.RTableValid R

properties.statement: The checks on a table as read give exactly the verdict of the checks on the table it loads as (every non-finite value written NaN): the model identifies NaN and ±Inf nowhere a verdict depends on it.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (R : Esm.Closed.Tables.RTable Esm.Closed.Tables.Lit), Esm.Closed.Tables.validateRaw R = Esm.Closed.Tables.validateTable R.load

properties.statement: Q-106: a document with a function_tables entry that fails one of the ten checks does not load, whether or not any lookup references it and whatever its expressions hold.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (d : Esm.Closed.Tables.Doc) (p : String × Esm.Closed.Tables.RTable Esm.Closed.Tables.Lit) (c : Esm.Closed.Code), p ∈ d.tables → Esm.Closed.Tables.validateRaw p.2 = Except.error c → ∃ (c' : Esm.Closed.Code), Esm.Closed.Tables.loadCheck d = Except.error c'

properties.statement: Q-106: a document loads iff every function_tables entry passes the ten checks and every node of every expression passes its load check (interp.* arguments, table_lookup checks).
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (d : Esm.Closed.Tables.Doc), Esm.Closed.Tables.loadCheck d = Except.ok () ↔ (∀ p ∈ d.tables, Esm.Closed.Tables.validateRaw p.2 = Except.ok ()) ∧ ∀ e ∈ d.exprs, ∀ n ∈ Esm.Closed.Tables.nodes e, Esm.Closed.Tables.checkNode d.loaded n = Except.ok ()

properties.statement: Q-106: a table_lookup node anywhere in an expression that fails its checks makes the document fail to load.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (d : Esm.Closed.Tables.Doc) (e : Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr), e ∈ d.exprs → ∀ (tid : String) (axes : List (String × Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr)) (out : Option Esm.Closed.Tables.OutSel) (args : List Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr) (c : Esm.Closed.Code), Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr.lookup tid axes out args ∈ Esm.Closed.Tables.nodes e → Esm.Closed.Tables.prepLookup d.loaded tid (List.map Prod.fst axes) out args = Except.error c → ∃ (c' : Esm.Closed.Code), Esm.Closed.Tables.loadCheck d = Except.error c'

properties.statement: Q-107: a table_lookup is table_lookup_unknown_table if it names no table; else the first failing check of its table (any args, keys, output); else table_lookup_args_nonempty if it has args; else (keys matching) the output check.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (tables : List (String × Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable)) (env : String → Esm.Closed.Num) (tid : String) (axes : List (String × Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr)) (out : Option Esm.Closed.Tables.OutSel) (args : List Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr), (List.lookup tid tables = Option.none → Esm.Closed.Tables.eval tables env (Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr.lookup tid axes out args) = Except.error "table_lookup_unknown_table") ∧ (∀ (T0 : Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable) (c : Esm.Closed.Code), List.lookup tid tables = Option.some T0 → Esm.Closed.Tables.validateTable T0 = Except.error c → Esm.Closed.Tables.eval tables env (Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr.lookup tid axes out args) = Except.error c) ∧ (∀ (T0 : Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable), List.lookup tid tables = Option.some T0 → Esm.Closed.Tables.validateTable T0 = Except.ok () → args ≠ [] → Esm.Closed.Tables.eval tables env (Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr.lookup tid axes out args) = Except.error "table_lookup_args_nonempty") ∧ ∀ (T0 : Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable) (c : Esm.Closed.Code), List.lookup tid tables = Option.some T0 → Esm.Closed.Tables.validateTable T0 = Except.ok () → Esm.Closed.Tables.keysMatch (List.map Prod.fst axes) (List.map (fun (x : Esm.Closed.Tables.Axis) => x.name) T0.axes) = Bool.true → Esm.Closed.Tables.resolveOutput T0 out = Except.error c → Esm.Closed.Tables.eval tables env (Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr.lookup tid axes out []) = Except.error c
properties.supersedes: P-tables-lookup-args-nonempty, which checked args before the table reference and the table (Q-107).

properties.statement: Q-113: a document with a failing function table is reported with the code of one of its failing tables, whatever its expression nodes hold.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (d : Esm.Closed.Tables.Doc), (∃ p ∈ d.tables, ∃ (c : Esm.Closed.Code), Esm.Closed.Tables.validateRaw p.2 = Except.error c) → ∃ p ∈ d.tables, ∃ (c : Esm.Closed.Code), Esm.Closed.Tables.validateRaw p.2 = Except.error c ∧ Esm.Closed.Tables.loadCheck d = Except.error c

properties.statement: The lookup check on tables as read (checkLookupRaw, which the esm-lean tables adapter runs at Float) is the exact model's prepLookup on the tables they load as.
properties.lean_statement: ∀ (tables : List (String × Esm.Closed.Tables.RTable Esm.Closed.Tables.Lit)) (tid : String) (keys : List String) (out : Option Esm.Closed.Tables.OutSel) (args : List Esm.Closed.Tables.Expr), Esm.Closed.Tables.checkLookupRaw tables tid keys out args.length = Except.map (fun (_ : Esm.Closed.Tables.FTable × Esm.Closed.Tables.Nested) => ()) (Esm.Closed.Tables.prepLookup (List.map (fun (p : String × Esm.Closed.Tables.RTable Esm.Closed.Tables.Lit) => (p.1, p.2.load)) tables) tid keys out args)
